h: Before the first frame in Cardiff
p: The Friary is a couple of minutes from Cardiff Queen Street station, which makes it handy for anyone travelling in from the Valleys lines, and Cardiff Central isn't far either. On match days the city gets very busy, with road closures around the stadium, so the train is often the easiest way to get in and out.

If you're booking for a group, think about lane numbers. Big groups usually have more fun across two lanes rather than crammed onto one, and it keeps the turns moving. Bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly check. Arriving ten minutes early means you can grab a drink and get settled before your slot starts.

Queen Street is Cardiff's main shopping street, and you'll find a statue of Aneurin Bevan, the Welsh politician who founded the NHS, standing along it. It's a nice photo stop. St David's shopping centre and the Capitol Centre are close by too, and the Cardiff Market off St Mary Street is a great place for Welsh cakes, cockles and a cuppa.

For a quieter break, Cathays Park, just north of the centre, is home to the City Hall and National Museum Cardiff, all set around grand white Portland stone buildings and leafy lawns. Alexandra Gardens, with its Welsh National War Memorial, is a peaceful spot to sit for a while before heading back to the lanes for a rematch.
